observations.contract: Separate tactical and animation clocks; qualification of earlier timeline
observations.trace: Current tactical networking declares TACTICAL_TICK_HZ=30 and installs Time<Fixed> at that rate. The authored locomotion sample rate is64Hz; ObservedMeleeStart independently derives its sample word by rounding elapsed Time multiplied by that rate, while melee authority uses its CombatInstant derived from elapsed Time. In the earlier rejected-contact hypothetical, 0,8,24,32,40 must be interpreted as animation sample coordinates, not 30Hz fixed updates. Eight sample steps correspond to 0.125 seconds only if the hypothetical start times are chosen on the stated sample boundaries; rounded sample IDs alone do not establish exact elapsed times or scheduler observations.
observations.remaining: The original hypothetical is preserved and now explicitly qualified rather than rewritten. No timed event or gameplay ran. Actual update cadence, admitted weapons, lunge, time quantization and conditional defense policy remain unresolved.

observations.contract: Iteration historical and current tick count
observations.trace: Frozen6533 iteration.rs used a local64Hz constant;95e imports the shared30Hz tactical constant. On loop exhaustion, both versions initialize final_tick to maximum_ticks and return final_tick+1 after executing the exclusive range. At95e the prior independently recorded source arithmetic is5400 updates versus5401 reported, conditional on no defeat. Early termination at zero-based tick k reports k+1.
observations.remaining: No iteration or report ran; actual timeout reachability and fixed-schedule count remain open. Historical64Hz bytes and earlier c100/95e observations are distinct and must not be substituted.

observations.contract: Iteration build admission and local sentinels
observations.trace: MeleeIterationBuild publicly exposes weapon_id, armor_ids, shield_id and combatant. The feature-gated public resolve_tactical_server_melee_duel receives a borrowed build. spawn_weapon checks combatant.equipment.melee_weapon and then expects item_catalog::definition(build.weapon_id), while definition returns Option. A caller able to supply a build with Some melee weapon and an unknown ID can reach this expect if prior app setup/catalog initialization succeed. The normal private roster builder calls fallible authored_equipment to bind its IDs and combatant, but public fields can subsequently diverge.
observations.remaining: No public caller, constructed build, app, catalog lookup or panic was run. External API use and viable earlier setup remain conditional. Fix admission at the actual build/API boundary without conflating normal roster construction with arbitrary caller input.

observations.contract: Retained iteration log resource and geometry
observations.trace: tactical_iteration_app inserts IterationLog; the duel later removes it with unwrap. Selected iteration source text contains no other removal. Equipment items retain authored IDs while armor projection copies first protected-part aggregate values; log consumers expose names and anatomical text after typed events.
observations.remaining: The resource unwrap violates the production rule but no missing-resource panic is established. Actual observer lifetime, overlapping roster armor, name policy and other previously indexed contracts remain open and separate.
